transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and just can’t keep up or focus at work anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm really struggling to get through my shifts.
Beyond feeling physically drained, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you previously enjoyed, or do you feel a persistent sense of sadness or hopelessness?

Yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling like a dark cloud is sitting on my chest, and I just feel sad and hopeless for no clear reason. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like jogging and working on my Raspberry Pi projects. Now, I just end up sitting on the couch scrolling through my phone because I can't bring myself to do anything else.
Have you experienced similar episodes of feeling this way in the past, or is this the very first time you have felt like this?

No, I've never felt this way before; this is the very first time. It all started about two years ago with the stress of a major electronic record upgrade at my clinic and starting my evening classes, and it has just been building up since then. Before that, I was doing completely fine.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since these feelings began two years ago?

Yes, both have changed a lot. I lie awake for hours worrying about work and being watched, then wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning unable to fall back asleep. My appetite has also dropped so much that I throw away most of my lunch, and my scrubs are actually hanging loose on me now.
Are you still able to perform your basic daily tasks and go to work, or have you reached a point where you are completely unable to function or participate in your usual activities?

I'm still barely forcing myself to go to work, but it takes all my energy and I just collapse on the couch the moment I get home. My performance has really slipped; I've been written up twice for charting errors and had to drop one of my evening classes. I've also completely stopped seeing friends or doing my hobbies like jogging because I'm just too drained.
During these past two years, have you ever felt that others were intentionally monitoring you, talking about you, or that you were being watched in a way that felt unusual or suspicious?

Yes, for about a year and a half now, I’ve been convinced that the new charting system at work was designed specifically to track my mistakes so administration can quietly build a case to pull my license. This thought keeps my mind spinning at night, even though my supervisor keeps reassuring me that it’s not personal.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around, or see things that other people cannot see?

Yes, pretty often when I'm alone at home or on late shifts, I hear a low male voice right behind me saying things like "You're screwing this up again" or "They know you're dangerous." I don't see anything at all, but hearing that voice feels incredibly real and unsettling.

Did you experience the periods of intense sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest at the same time as the thoughts about being watched and the voices, or did the mood symptoms occur only after the suspicious thoughts and voices began?

Yes, they actually happened at the same time. The low mood and loss of interest really ramped up right when I started hearing the voice and feeling like the charting system was targeting me, so they've pretty much gone hand-in-hand most of this time.

During these past two years, have there been any periods where you experienced the suspicious thoughts and voices while your mood felt relatively normal, or have the depressive symptoms been present for the vast majority of the time that you have been experiencing these psychotic symptoms?

For the vast majority of the last two years, that heavy, hopeless feeling has been there constantly, except for a few brief times when I felt more numb than sad. However, there was a stretch late last summer when my mood lifted a bit and I didn't feel particularly depressed, but I still heard the voice and believed the charting system was tracking me.
During that stretch last summer when your mood felt better, how long did those psychotic symptoms—the voice and the belief about being tracked—persist without any significant depressive symptoms?

That stretch lasted for about three or four weeks where I didn't feel especially depressed. Even though my mood was better during those weeks, the voice and the belief that the system was tracking me persisted the entire time.

During that three-to-four-week period when your mood was better, did you experience any other significant symptoms, such as feeling unusually energetic, having a decreased need for sleep, or feeling like your thoughts were racing?

No, I didn't experience any high energy, racing thoughts, or a decreased need for sleep during that time; I just felt a bit more level and numb rather than intensely depressed. Even though my mood was slightly better, the paranoia about the charting system tracking me and that critical male voice still continued just as before.

Critically, the patient described a period of 3-4 weeks where psychotic symptoms persisted in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, but without evidence of mania or hypomania. This duration of psychosis without mood symptoms (greater than 2 weeks) satisfies the criteria for schizoaffective disorder, specifically the depressive type, while ruling out mood disorders with psychotic features. F25.0 is excluded because the patient explicitly denied any manic or hypomanic symptoms during the interview.
